questions.question: Which of the following cartilages forms a complete ring?

suspectLines.text: Cricoid cartilage forms a complete ring around the airway and is the only laryngeal cartilage to do so.

questions.explanation:
Cricoid cartilage forms a complete ring around the airway and is the only laryngeal cartilage to do so.

Clinical significance: in Sellick manoeuvre, cricoid pressure is applied to occlude the esophagus without occluding the airway, helping prevent regurgitation of gastric contents during rapid induction. The cricoid is also the narrowest part of the pediatric airway.
